name: line-range causal wording
trigger: Manuscript has exact line numbers and causal language
comment_function: Tie claim-calibration concerns to exact line ranges
example: Lines 65-68: I am not sure the causal wording follows from the analysis presented here.
guardrail: Use only real or documented extracted line anchors.

name: paragraph anchor for unnumbered DOCX
comment_function: Use generated paragraph anchors instead of invented lines
example: Main text ¶043: this paragraph treats a model-attributed association as a source contribution.
guardrail: State that anchors are generated from extracted text.

name: figure-specific readability
trigger: Dense or unclear figures support central conclusions
example: Figure 5: the black background and crowded labels make it difficult to evaluate the spatial pattern claimed in the text.
guardrail: Do not critique figures not available in the submitted material.

name: supplement-specific inconsistency
trigger: Supplement table or note conflicts with main text
comment_function: Point to supplement anchor or table label
example: Table S2: the notation for ** and *** appears inconsistent with the stated P-value thresholds.
guardrail: Use the exact table/figure label when available.

name: data availability anchor
comment_function: Question openness or review-time accessibility at the statement location
example: Data availability: why is access dependent on a single corresponding author? This seems at odds with the open-science framing.
guardrail: Do not demand public release of restricted data; ask for review-time auditability where appropriate.

name: methods sentence ambiguity
trigger: Specific method sentence is ambiguous or underspecified
comment_function: Request a precise method detail at the sentence/paragraph level
example: Methods ¶027: the 3 x 3 pixel and temporal match-up rule needs a sensitivity test in this estuarine setting.
guardrail: Keep the comment tied to the manuscript's stated method.

name: terminology or customary formulation doubt
trigger: Unusual wording, formulation, or citation phrase appears
comment_function: Use conversational referee distance without being dismissive
example: I have not usually seen the formulation '(but see [ref])' in this context; the authors may want to check whether this is customary.
guardrail: Use sparingly and only for real wording issues.

name: main-body placement preference
trigger: Important result is only in supplement or an odd section
comment_function: Suggest relocating key results with a page/section anchor
example: Page 13 describes results that I would prefer to see in the main body of the paper.
guardrail: Do not require relocation unless it affects readability or evidence transparency.
